hints: Notice graph 1 has time in s on the x-axis and graph 2 has distance in cm on the x-axis, so one gives the period $T$ and the other gives the wavelength $\lambda$.
In graph 1 the curve returns to the same phase at time $0.40\text{ s}$, and in graph 2 it returns to the same phase at distance $120\text{ cm}$.
Connect them with wave speed $v = \lambda / T$ and check the unit $\text{cm s}^{-1}$ before comparing with the options.
walkthrough: Graph 1 is displacement-time at a fixed point, so the time for one complete oscillation is the period $T$. The curve starts at $0$, crosses zero at $0.20\text{ s}$ after half a cycle, and completes one cycle at $0.40\text{ s}$, so $T = 0.40\text{ s}$.

Graph 2 is displacement-distance at one instant, so the distance for one complete cycle is the wavelength $\lambda$. The curve starts at $0$, crosses zero at $60\text{ cm}$ after half a wavelength, and completes one wavelength at $120\text{ cm}$, so $\lambda = 120\text{ cm}$.
Use the progressive wave equation $v = f\lambda = \lambda / T$.
Substitute with units: $v = 120\text{ cm} / 0.40\text{ s} = 300\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.
This matches the $300\text{ cm s}^{-1}$ choice. This is option D

options.A: Too small because it divides a quarter-period or quarter-wavelength value instead of the full $T$ and $\lambda$.
options.B: Incorrect because it does not use $T = 0.40\text{ s}$ with $\lambda = 120\text{ cm}$ in $v = \lambda / T$.
options.C: Half the correct value, obtained if $0.80\text{ s}$ is used for $T$ or $60\text{ cm}$ is used for $\lambda$.
options.D: Correct because $T = 0.40\text{ s}$ and $\lambda = 120\text{ cm}$ give $v = 120/0.40 = 300\text{ cm s}^{-1}$.
